text: 🚨🇲🇽 "I'd like to hear or see a report on what the U.S. government does inside the United States." Asked about a U.S. report tying Mexican officials to organized crime, President Sheinbaum turned it around: what is Washington doing about its own consumption? — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the U.S. drug report She called drug use a public health crisis fed by opioids "from medicines that were approved even though it was known they would cause addiction."

🇲🇽🌎 "That poll has no basis in reality — that is false." A U.S. outlet claimed most Mexicans favor a foreign intervention. Sheinbaum: it doesn't even name a source, and professional polling shows the opposite. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on the intervention poll "Foreign interventions don't help, and sovereignty is lost." It would contradict, she said, the national pride seen worldwide on the night of the Grito.

🇲🇽♻️ "I recycle my clothes." Asked about her wardrobe, President Sheinbaum said she reuses her clothing — mends pieces with seamstresses and wears garments made by Mexican artisans — rather than buying new. — Claudia Sheinbaum, at the mañanera

🇲🇽🎨 "There is nothing more beautiful than this — Mexican artisans, women and men." FONART buys directly from artisans at cost and returns the money straight to them — instead of the old scheme where they were haggled down and their work resold elsewhere for more. — Claudia Sheinbaum, on Mexican artisans

🇲🇽🔔 Saturday, Sept 19: Mexico's second national drill — a seismic alert to more than 80 million cell phones. The nationwide exercise simulates a 7.7 earthquake with epicenter in Tehuacán, Puebla, across all 32 states, in memory of the 1985 and 2017 quakes. — Laura Velázquez, National Civil Protection For the first time at this scale, the alert reaches phones directly. On keeping the same alarm tone: "The drill should be a drill in every sense."

🇲🇽🚆 3,161 km of priority roads — built by the state, not handed to private concessions. Mexico's 2025-2030 highway program: 154.6 billion pesos, about 177,000 direct jobs, and 82% of materials and services from Mexican suppliers. — Program presented at the mañanera, Sept 17 Under the "mixed investment" model, public and private funds build the roads — but the highways are not turned over to private operators.

🇲🇽📈 <u>Mexico posts its biggest half-year of foreign investment ever</u>

Even under Trump's tariff threats, Mexico drew a record $34.968 billion in foreign direct investment in the first half of 2026 — the highest first-half figure ever recorded, up nearly 90% in five years, per the Economy Ministry. The US is still the top source at $16.9bn (48.2%), and 88.5% was reinvested profits: firms already here doubling down, not leaving. Mexico now ranks among the world's ten biggest FDI destinations — ahead of India, France, Spain and Italy.

🇲🇽🗳️ <u>PAN moves to lock Morena's Santiago Nieto out of Querétaro's Congress</u>

In PAN-governed Querétaro, the panista head of the state Congress moved to physically bar Santiago Nieto — Morena's coordinator for the defense of the Fourth Transformation — from entering the chamber. Nieto called it "inadmissible in democratic terms… a personalized gag order, a display of authoritarianism and repression against the advance of Morena and the 4T," and vowed to challenge it "to the last consequences."

🔥🇲🇽 <u>Declassified files: the PRI's secret police even spied on its own</u>

Newly surfaced DFS archives — Mexico's Cold-War political police, with reports signed by spymasters like Miguel Nazar Haro — show the old regime didn't just hunt dissidents: from 1975 it tracked the "loyalty" of its own rising figures, logging a young Roberto Madrazo's rallies as it vetted him for the machine. The surveillance state the PRI sold to Mexico as democracy.

🇲🇽🌱 <u>Mexico seals a beachfront build that bulldozed protected dunes</u>

Federal inspectors from Profepa shut down a construction site in Chabihau, Yucatán after heavy machinery destroyed 669 m² of protected coastal dune — tearing out threatened button mangrove and wild cotton, habitat of a threatened iguana — with zero environmental authorization. "Those responsible did not exhibit any authorization, permit, license or environmental exemption," the agency reported, placing seals on the works under NOM-022.
